        "title": "Enforce query depth and complexity limits",
        "given": "a public GraphQL endpoint accepting nested queries",
        "when": "a client submits a query",
        "then": "the server rejects queries exceeding a defined depth/cost limit before execution"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Production introspection reveals full schema to anyone",
      "scenario": "An attacker queries the public endpoint's introspection system to enumerate every type, field and relationship (including customer profile fields), mapping the entire data model to plan further attacks without any authentication.",
      "component": "GraphQL endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Introspection is enabled in production."}],
      "asvs": ["V14.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can ask the API to list its entire internal data structure, handing attackers a map of what to target.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Disable introspection in production",
        "given": "a production GraphQL deployment",
        "when": "a client sends an introspection query",
        "then": "the server does not return schema details to unauthenticated or public clients"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Customer profiles exposed through nested queries without access control",
      "scenario": "Because the endpoint is public and nested queries can traverse from products/reviews into customer profiles, an attacker crafts a query that pulls other customers' profile data (names, emails, order history) they have no right to see, with no authentication required.",
      "component": "GraphQL endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Clients can request nested queries of products, reviews and customer profiles."}, {"quote": "GraphQL API for the storefront"}],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "A stranger could ask for other customers' personal details by chaining a product or review query into their profile, with no login needed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce field-level authorization on customer profile data",
        "given": "a GraphQL query that resolves into customer profile fields",
        "when": "the requester is unauthenticated or lacks ownership of that profile",
        "then": "the server omits or denies access to those fields"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Query aliasing/batching allows brute-force and amplification",
      "scenario": "An attacker sends a single request containing many aliased copies of the same nested query (products/reviews/customer profiles), multiplying backend load and effectively bypassing simple per-request rate limits in one call.",
      "component": "GraphQL endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Clients can request nested queries of products, reviews and customer profiles."}],
      "asvs": ["V13.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "A single request can be crafted to secretly repeat itself hundreds of times, overwhelming the backend behind one normal-looking call.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit query cost including aliases and batching",
        "given": "a GraphQL request with aliased or batched operations",
        "when": "the computed cost exceeds the allowed threshold",
        "then": "the server rejects the request before executing resolvers"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "No authentication on public API allows unrestricted data mutation/traversal surface",
      "scenario": "Since the endpoint is public with no authentication layer described, any client reaching the GraphQL API can probe and traverse mutations/queries that should be restricted to logged-in customers or staff, increasing the attack surface for write operations if any exist alongside reads.",
      "component": "GraphQL endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "The storefront uses a public GraphQL endpoint."}],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "The API is open to the internet with no sign-in check described, so anyone could try operations meant only for logged-in users.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require authentication for non-public operations",
        "given": "a GraphQL operation that reads or writes customer or order data",
        "when": "the request has no valid session/token",
        "then": "the server rejects the operation"
      }
    }
  ]
